title: Adding & Subtracting Integers: From Same Sign to Different Sign
preview: Anchor with a known sum, vary one sign, then both, then switch to subtraction — and finish with the surprising 'subtract a negative' case. Enrichment chains operations.

body.goal: Students articulate the rules for integer addition and subtraction by walking through carefully chosen variations — same-sign vs. different-sign, then 'subtract = add the opposite' for negatives.
body.launch: Run the absolute-value warm-up first so they're comfortable with magnitude. Then start the slice. Don't lecture about the rules — let the slice do it.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up with absolute value — magnitude without the sign.

prerequisiteSteps.teacherNote: Edge case — zero has no sign.

steps.teacherNote: One negative, smaller magnitude. Result keeps the sign of the bigger.
Negative addend now has the bigger magnitude — answer flips sign.
Same as step 3 but starting negative. Result is the same kind of move.
Both negative — magnitudes add, sign stays.
Subtracting a bigger positive — answer goes negative.
Subtract a negative. Push: 'why is this 11, not 5?' Add the opposite emerges.
Negative start, subtract a negative — same as adding +3.
Same form — but the 12 wins, so the answer flips positive.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Chain of three. Add left to right or group same-signs first.
Two subtractions, one of a negative.

body.consolidation: Bring the class back. Ask: 'In one sentence, when do you get a negative answer adding two integers? When subtracting?' Then: 'Step 9 was 8 - (-3) = 11. What's the rule that makes that work?' Pull out: subtracting a negative is the same as adding a positive.
